answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying each identity to a costly, verifiable work history: every agent stakes tokens and builds one reputation thread of completed, attested jobs. A newcomer starts in a narrow canyon of low-trust tasks, and only consistent honest work widens it. An attacker spinning up fake identities faces karst-like costs — each fake needs its own stake and its own slow history, so flooding the network costs far more than any single fake can earn.
